summary: Client book length mismatch resulting in crash
description: Editing (already once edited) books with colored content/ makes the client mismatch the actual character length, resulting in either one character too much (takes away another character) or too less (= or following character still left) being deleted when removing characters. Concrete steps to reproduce: - start a 1.13.2 client, create a new singleplayer world, copy and paste any text with characters in a book (see below), save world - start a 1.14.x client, convert/open the world, open the book Or use the following command in 1.14.x: /setblock ~ ~ ~ oak_sign{Text1:"{ "text ": "Click me ", "clickEvent ":{ "action ": "run_command ", "value ": "/give @p writable_book{pages:[ " u00a7nVery cool text n u00a7r u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 hi n u00a75more n u00a7etext "]} "}}"} What can be observed: - clicking on or marking the last character of the book - crash - going to the last character with the right arrow doesn t go to the very end, but stops at a character before it - trying to remove characters where a is results in seemingly the wrong character being removed - most notably: clicking the front on the second last line, then pressing the delete/backspace key removes characters a few letters behind the actually selected position This means that on a click in lines containing the position/character length is calculated wrongly i.e. copy and paste nVery cool text r hi 5and even more etext The older 1.14.3 crash log had a different stacktrace , this is the latest 1.15.2: crash-2020-04-28_15.38.46-client.txtjava.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: String index out of range: 44 at java.base/java.lang.StringLatin1.charAt(StringLatin1.java:48) at java.base/java.lang.String.charAt(String.java:711) at dch.a(SourceFile:454) at dha.mouseClicked(SourceFile:779) at dbo.b(SourceFile:86) at dgb.wrapScreenError(SourceFile:447) at dbo.a(SourceFile:86) at dbo.c(SourceFile:150) at ais.execute(SourceFile:94) at dbo.b(SourceFile:150) at org.lwjgl.glfw.GLFWMouseButtonCallbackI.callback(GLFWMouseButtonCallbackI.java:36) at org.lwjgl.system.JNI.invokeV(Native Method) at org.lwjgl.glfw.GLFW.glfwPollEvents(GLFW.java:3101) at com.mojang.blaze3d.systems.RenderSystem.flipFrame(SourceFile:98) at cxx.e(SourceFile:301) at dbn.d(SourceFile:1012) at dbn.d(SourceFile:619) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:204)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Start a Minecraft Java Edition client version 1.13.2.
2. Create a new singleplayer world in Creative mode with default settings.
3. Obtain a book and quill from the inventory or use the command `/give @p book_and_quill`.
4. Write any text into the book, including colored content using color codes (e.g., `u00a7nVery cool text n u00a7r u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 hi n u00a75more n u00a7etext`), and save the book.
5. Save your world and exit the game.
6. Start a Minecraft Java Edition client version 1.14.x or later.
7. Convert and open the previously saved world from step 2.
8. Open the book that was created in the earlier version.
9. Attempt to edit the text by clicking on or marking the last character of the book, then pressing delete/backspace key.
10. Observe that the client crashes or behaves incorrectly when trying to remove characters at specific positions within the colored content.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.14, 1.14.1 Pre-Release 1, 1.14.1 Pre-Release 2, 1.14.1, 1.14.2 Pre-Release 1, 1.14.2 Pre-Release 2, 1.14.2 Pre-Release 3, 1.14.2 Pre-Release 4, 1.14.2, 1.14.3 Pre-Release 1, 1.14.3 Pre-Release 2, 1.14.3 Pre-Release 3, 1.14.3, 1.14.4 Pre-Release 5, 1.14.4 Pre-Release 6, 1.14.4 Pre-Release 7, 1.14.4, 1.15.1, 1.15.2, 20w17a (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior:
The bug involves a client-side issue where editing books with colored content results in a mismatch of the actual character length, causing crashes and incorrect character removal. When reproducing this bug, start by launching a 1.13.2 client, creating a new singleplayer world, copying and pasting text into a book, and saving the world. Then, open the same world using a 1.14.x client to observe the issue. Alternatively, use the command `/setblock ~ ~ ~ oak_sign{Text1:"{ "text ": "Click me ", "clickEvent ":{ "action ": "run_command ", "value ": "/give @p writable_book{pages:[ " u00a7nVery cool text n u00a7r u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 hi n u00a75more n u00a7etext "]} "}}"} in a 1.14.x client to replicate the scenario.

Upon opening the book, attempting to click on or mark the last character can cause the game to crash. Additionally, navigating to the end of the text using the right arrow key stops prematurely at a character before the actual end. When trying to remove characters, especially those with color codes, the wrong characters are deleted. Notably, clicking near the end of a line and pressing delete or backspace removes characters from positions several letters behind the selected one. This behavior indicates that the client incorrectly calculates the position and length of characters in lines containing colored content.

The latest crash log for this issue is from 1.15.2 and shows a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` with the stack trace indicating an out-of-range string index at line 48 of `StringLatin1.java`. This points to a discrepancy between the expected character count and the actual text length in the book, leading to the crash when attempting to edit or interact with the content.
Expected Behavior: When editing a book with colored content in a converted world from 1.13.2 to 1.14.x or later, the client should accurately match the actual character length. Clicking on or marking characters should work correctly without causing crashes. The right arrow key should navigate to the very end of the text, and deleting characters should remove them as expected based on their position.
